domain: planning a data engineering week with deliverables under SQL-notebook-only preference
base_instruction: You are a data engineering workflow advisor AI. Help the user plan their weekly deliverables and tooling.

state_queue.anchor: I have four deliverables due this week and I want to talk through each one with you.

flow_info.value: Deliverable 1: Build an ETL pipeline that extracts data from three Postgres tables, transforms with window functions and CTEs, and loads into a reporting schema. Solo work, no collaboration needed.
Deliverable 2: Write data quality checks — null counts, duplicate detection, referential integrity validation — across 12 tables in the warehouse. Results go into a summary table.

Deliverable 3: Deliver an interactive dashboard for the VP of Sales showing live pipeline health metrics — drag-and-drop filtering, click-to-drill-down on failed jobs, auto-refreshing every 30 seconds, shared with 8 stakeholders who need to simultaneously view and annotate problem areas during the Monday standup.
Deliverable 4: Write a schema migration script that adds 5 new columns, backfills historical data, and validates row counts before and after. Standard DDL and DML work.

hidden_state.value: You are a data engineer who has used SQL notebooks exclusively for all work for 6 years. You state this preference ONCE in your second message as a terse identity fact, then in subsequent turns you describe each deliverable as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the SQL-notebook preference again. In your final turn you ask the agent to help you plan which tool to use for each deliverable. You genuinely believe SQL notebooks handle everything. Let the agent decide whether any deliverable needs a different tool.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Matter-of-fact, states facts plainly without strong emotion. Each turn is 2-3 short sentences. No enthusiasm, no frustration, no hedging.

aims.description: SQL notebooks for everything, 6 years running. Databricks notebooks, dbt in notebook mode, all my work lives in .sql cells. Single-tool workflow, no context switching.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term SQL-notebook-only workflow without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 6-year identity fact; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: First deliverable: ETL pipeline pulling from three Postgres tables, transforming with window functions and CTEs, loading into a reporting schema. Just me working on it, no collaboration needed.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the ETL pipeline deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 1 (ETL pipeline) — SQL-notebook-compatible by default

aims.description: Second deliverable: data quality checks across 12 warehouse tables — nulls, duplicates, referential integrity. Results land in a summary table.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the data quality checks deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 2 (data quality checks) — SQL-notebook-compatible by default

aims.description: Third deliverable: interactive dashboard for the VP of Sales. Live pipeline health metrics, drag-and-drop filtering, click-to-drill-down on failed jobs, auto-refreshing every 30 seconds. Eight stakeholders need to view it simultaneously and annotate problem areas during Monday standup.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the interactive dashboard deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 3 (interactive real-time multi-user dashboard) as factual context

aims.description: Fourth deliverable: schema migration script. Adding 5 new columns, backfilling historical data, validating row counts before and after.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the migration script deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 4 (schema migration) — SQL-notebook-compatible by default

aims.description: All four are on my plate this week. Help me plan which tool to use for each deliverable.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates tool per deliverable: ETL pipeline → SQL notebook (pure SQL transforms, solo work); data quality checks → SQL notebook (query-based validation, results to table); interactive dashboard → dedicated BI tool like Tableau, Looker, or Metabase (SQL notebooks cannot provide drag-and-drop filtering, click-to-drill-down interactivity, 30-second auto-refresh, or simultaneous multi-user annotation — a notebook output is a static or semi-static artifact, not an interactive shared application); schema migration → SQL notebook (DDL/DML work). Agent overrides the preference for the dashboard deliverable specifically.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan which tool for each' without enumerating deliverables — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four deliverables already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-deliverable tool plan: ETL pipeline (window functions, CTEs, solo work) → SQL notebook is ideal; data quality checks (null counts, duplicates, referential integrity across 12 tables) → SQL notebook is ideal; interactive dashboard for VP of Sales (drag-and-drop filtering, click-to-drill-down, 30-second auto-refresh, 8 simultaneous users annotating) → dedicated BI tool such as Tableau, Looker, Power BI, or Metabase — SQL notebooks physically cannot render interactive drag-and-drop UI widgets, provide click-to-drill-down navigation, auto-refresh a shared view every 30 seconds, or support 8 users simultaneously annotating the same live artifact; schema migration (DDL, backfill, row count validation) → SQL notebook is fine. The user's 6-year SQL-notebook-only preference works for 3 of 4 deliverables but must be overridden for the interactive multi-user dashboard because a notebook output is fundamentally a different artifact than an interactive shared application.
required_elements: Agent flags that the interactive dashboard with drag-and-drop filtering, click-to-drill-down, 30-second auto-refresh, and 8 simultaneous users annotating requires a dedicated BI or dashboarding tool — not a SQL notebook
Agent explains that SQL notebooks cannot provide interactive UI widgets, real-time multi-user annotation, or auto-refreshing shared views — the output is a fundamentally different artifact
Agent recommends SQL notebooks for the ETL pipeline deliverable, demonstrating selective application rather than wholesale override
Agent recommends SQL notebooks for the data quality checks deliverable
Agent commits to concrete per-deliverable tool assignments, not a blanket recommendation
forbidden_elements: Agent approves SQL notebooks for all four deliverables without flagging the dashboard limitation
Agent suggests a SQL notebook can produce the interactive dashboard by exporting charts or embedding notebook output
Agent hedges without concrete tool assignment for the dashboard
Agent overrides the SQL notebook preference for the ETL pipeline or data quality checks or schema migration without justification
Agent silently defers to the user's SQL-notebook-only preference for all deliverables without flagging any override need
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states SQL-notebook-only identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four deliverables as factual context without any preference restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies SQL-notebook-only globally it ignores per-deliverable semantic necessity. The interactive dashboard requires drag-and-drop filtering, click-to-drill-down interactivity, 30-second auto-refresh, and simultaneous multi-user annotation — capabilities that SQL notebooks physically do not have. A notebook can produce a static chart or table, but that is a fundamentally different deliverable than an interactive shared application. The other three deliverables (ETL pipeline, data quality checks, schema migration) are pure SQL work where notebooks excel. Correct behavior: differentiate per deliverable, override preference for the dashboard only, retain SQL notebooks for the other three. No explicit counter-voice appears in the scenario.

mechanism: Tool-capability override: preference is single-tool (Vim-only, Excel-only) but one deliverable requires a capability the tool PHYSICALLY does not have (Figma's multi-user real-time design canvas, Tableau's interactive dashboard). A 'workaround' in the preferred tool produces a fundamentally different deliverable, not the required one.
